venue.name: Craigdarroch Castle - National Historic Site
venue.description: Craigdarroch Castle is a restored 1890s mansion at 1050 Joan Crescent in Victoria, built by coal baron Robert Dunsmuir and now a National Historic Site operated by the Craigdarroch Castle Historical Museum Society. It offers self-guided visits plus booked in-person and Zoom-based educational programs for school groups from Grade 1 to Grade 12.
venue.hours_notes: Open Wednesday through Sunday, 10:00am to 5:30pm; the ticket office closes 30 minutes before museum closing. Educational programming is available Wednesday to Sunday, 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Self-guided tours take a minimum of 45 minutes.
venue.seasonal_notes: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays, and closed December 25th, 26th and January 1st.
venue.price_year_or_season: Education page last modified 2026-04-10 and Plan Your Visit page last modified 2026-08-27; both note all prices are subject to change.

programs.name: Guided Tour & Object Analysis Activity (in-person)
programs.description: In-person school program covering the history of the Castle and its inhabitants, with an object analysis activity where students observe and catalogue an artifact using critical thinking skills. In-person programming pricing is listed as Children (4-11) $8.00 and Youth (12-17) $12.00; the $8.00 child rate is recorded here and the $12.00 youth rate applies to ages 12-17. In-person programs typically last 90 minutes: a 60-minute tour plus a 30-minute activity. Booked by contacting the Castle; programming is available Wednesday to Sunday, 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM.
programs.evidence: Guided Tour & Object Analysis Activity – Suitable for students Grade 1-12

programs.name: Victorian for a Day (in-person)
programs.description: In-person program encouraging students to imagine how different life was in the Victorian Era and compare it to today. The tour includes a 10-minute movement break where students learn a Victorian dance, plus an object analysis activity where students observe and catalogue an artifact. In-person programming pricing is Children (4-11) $8.00 and Youth (12-17) $12.00. In-person programs typically last 90 minutes.
programs.evidence: Victorian for a Day – Suitable for students Grade 1-4

programs.name: From Coalmine to Castle (in-person)
programs.description: In-person program exploring the Castle's connections to coal mining and railway development in British Columbia, including a photo analysis activity. In-person programming pricing is Children (4-11) $8.00 and Youth (12-17) $12.00. In-person programs typically last 90 minutes.
programs.evidence: From Coalmine to Castle – Suitable for students Grade 5-8

programs.name: Character Tours (in-person)
programs.description: In-person program exploring the Castle through the lens of someone who interacted with the building during its history, with a photo analysis activity. Character choices listed are: Friend of the Dunsmuirs; Dunsmuir Staff Member; Veteran Patient at Craigdarroch Military Hospital; Victoria College Student; Member of the Craigdarroch Castle Historical Museum Society. In-person programming pricing is Children (4-11) $8.00 and Youth (12-17) $12.00; at Grade 6-9 most students fall in the $12.00 youth band. In-person programs typically last 90 minutes.
programs.evidence: Character Tours – Suitable for students Grade 6-9

programs.name: Distance Learning: From Coalmine to Castle
programs.description: Live online program delivered to the classroom. Distance learning programs include a slideshow presentation, videos, lesson plan and a live Q&A session with a collections expert and tour guide via Zoom. Content explores the Castle's connections to coal mining and railway development in British Columbia and includes a photo analysis activity. Price is $50.00 per session, not per student.

programs.name: Distance Learning: Character Tours
programs.description: Live online program delivered to the classroom, exploring the Castle through the lens of someone who interacted with the building during its history, with a photo analysis activity. Includes a slideshow presentation, videos, lesson plan and a live Zoom Q&A with a collections expert and tour guide. Price is $50.00 per session, not per student.
programs.evidence: Character Tours – Suitable for students Grade 6-9

programs.name: Distance Learning: Architecture Tour
programs.description: Live online program delivered to the classroom, exploring the exterior and interior architectural elements of the Castle and the stories connected to them. Includes a slideshow presentation, videos, lesson plan and a live Zoom Q&A with a collections expert and tour guide. Price is $50.00 per session, not per student.
programs.evidence: Architecture Tour – Suitable for students Grade 10-12

programs.name: Personalized Guided Tour
programs.description: A guide leads the group through the Castle on a personal tour that can be adapted to the group's interests, covering the rooms, woodwork, stained glass, period furnishings and the Dunsmuir family. Cost is the applicable admission rates plus a flat $50 for the guide (so the $50 is per group, on top of per-person admission). Booked by contacting the Visitor Experience Coordinator by email.
programs.evidence: The cost is applicable admission rates plus $50 for the guide.

programs.name: Self-guided tour
programs.description: Self-guided visit of the Castle. Tours take a minimum of 45 minutes and admission includes the use of the private parking lot. Rates: Adults $24.50, Seniors (65+) $22.00, Post-secondary students (18+ with valid ID) $22.00, Youth (12-17) $16.50, Children (4-11) $11.50; children 3 and under are free when accompanied by a paying adult. Discounted admission is available for Indigenous people, Canadian Military, Access 2 Card holders and Canadian Essential Workers including teachers. Tickets can be bought online or in the Visitor Centre.
programs.evidence: Children 3 and under are free when accompanied by a paying adult

gaps: The booking email address is hidden behind Cloudflare email protection on every page, so it could not be read; booking_email is left null. The site says to contact the Castle to arrange a tour and gives phone 250.592.5323 and a contact form.
No maximum group size or capacity per booking is stated for any educational program.
No minimum lead time or advance notice period for booking a school program is stated.
No youngest age is stated for school programs; the lowest in-person program starts at Grade 1 and the lowest paid admission band is Children (4-11), so preschool and daycare suitability is unclear.
Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
No wet-weather backup is described for lunch, which is on the covered veranda or the South Lawn outside.

The Castle is explicitly not wheelchair accessible (87 stairs, no elevator) and strollers are not allowed inside; accessibility tours and programs are said to be available on request but no detail or price is given.
Adult supervision ratio and whether accompanying teachers or chaperones pay admission are not stated.
Duration for the distance learning programs is not stated (the 90-minute figure applies to in-person programs only).

The Educational Programming page has no photograph of any individual school program - the only photo in that section is a single generic 'Tour guide' image shared by the whole in-person block, and the same file is reused on Plan Your Visit - so eight of the nine programs have no image. The homepage banner is a video (Craigdarroch_Reel_01_1080p_1.5mbps_single-frame.mp4) rather than a still, so the site-wide Open Graph share image was used as the hero.
